title: Shell Safety & Timeout Enforcement
scope: Map how OpenWorker's shell tool prevents LLM-generated commands from hanging the harness via persistent shell, non-interactive env, timeout bounds, and interrupt safety.

executor_pattern.persistent_shell: Keeps one long-lived shell process so cd, export, activated venvs persist across run_shell calls — unlike per-call subprocess.run
executor_pattern.os_native: POSIX: /bin/bash; Windows: powershell.exe (-Command - REPL). Each backend has its own marker/exit-code protocol
executor_pattern.interface_abc: Executor interface is the hedge for future ContainerExecutor/VMExecutor (sandboxing) without touching the engine

noninteractive_safety.purpose: Discourages commands from blocking on a prompt — LLM-generated commands that try to ask for input get non-interactive defaults instead of hanging forever

timeout_bounds.foreground_max: _MAX_TIMEOUT = 600.0s (10 min) — capped so a model-requested timeout can't wedge the turn
timeout_bounds.background: Background tasks (run_in_background) get their own detached process — NOT the persistent shell — so a dev server can run while the session keeps working

interrupt_safety.timeout_recovery: Timed-out command is interrupted (SIGINT to foreground child on POSIX, Ctrl-Break to child group on Windows); the shell survives so session state is preserved
interrupt_safety.background_persistence: Background tasks are NOT killed by close() (which the timeout-recovery path calls) — they end when they exit or via shell_task_kill
interrupt_safety.cancel_integration: TurnEngine.request_interrupt() cancels the asyncio Event AND runs interrupt_hooks — the shell executor's interrupt() is registered as a hook

risk_class.SHELL_TOOL: run_shell classified as RiskClass.EXEC — requires approval in INTERACTIVE mode
risk_class.command_operators: Shell metacharacters (;, &, |, >, <, `, $(), (, newlines) disqualify auto-run — approval required instead
risk_class.deny_by_default: In PLAN/DISCUSS modes, EXEC tools are hard-blocked; in INTERACTIVE mode they need user approval

gap_vs_ai_factory.subprocess_safety: factory/common/subprocess.py:41 — _run_proc() calls subprocess.run(argv, cwd=REPO_ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=TOOL_SUBPROCESS_TIMEOUT=300) but passes no _NONINTERACTIVE_ENV (no GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, PIP_NO_INPUT=1, DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive), no shell operator detection, and on TimeoutExpired (line 48) uses proc.kill() (SIGKILL at line 51) without SIGINT-first graceful recovery or ModelRetry context injection
gap_vs_ai_factory.tool_wrapper_safety: factory/common/subprocess.py:69 — _run_tool() wraps subprocess calls with error envelope at line 83 but adds no _NONINTERACTIVE_ENV, no shell operator detection, no ModelRetry on timeout — a hallucinated command blocking on input hangs until the 300s wall-clock cap then returns raw stderr without recovery guidance
gap_vs_ai_factory.missing_bash_wrapper: factory/tools/shell.py — dedicated bash tool wrapper (analogous to OpenWorker tools/shell.py with LocalExecutor) does not exist in ai-factory; the bash MCP tool is a built-in opencode tool with no ai-factory safety layer (no persistent shell, no _NONINTERACTIVE_ENV, no 120s/600s timeout bounds, no SIGINT-on-timeout recovery, no shell operator to approval gate)
gap_vs_ai_factory.no_risk_classification: No RiskClass (READ/WRITE_LOCAL/EXEC/EXTERNAL) + Mode (DISCUSS/PLAN/INTERACTIVE/AUTO) deny-by-default gate — factory/infra/tools_guard.py:357-361 TOOL_REGISTRY maps tool names to functions across read-only/AST-edit/CLI-wrapper buckets but has no permission gate; EXEC-level subprocess calls execute freely without approval in any mode, unlike OpenWorker risk.py + permissions.py

proposal: ai-factory's bash tool (built-in opencode MCP tool, executed via factory/common/subprocess.py:41) runs commands via subprocess.run with a 300s timeout but no _NONINTERACTIVE_ENV (GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, PIP_NO_INPUT=1), no shell operator detection (;, &, |, >, <, `, $(), newlines), and no SIGINT-on-timeout recovery (only SIGKILL via proc.kill()). When the LLM hallucinates a command that blocks on input (e.g. git commit without GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0), the command hangs until the 300s cap then is SIGKILLed without context recovery. OpenWorker's LocalExecutor pattern — persistent shell + _NONINTERACTIVE_ENV + 120s/600s timeout bounds + SIGINT-on-timeout + shell operator to approval gate — recovers the turn instead of crashing. A dedicated factory/tools/shell.py wrapper (analogous to OpenWorker's tools/shell.py) does not exist. Adopt: non-interactive env (GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, PIP_NO_INPUT=1), timeout bounds (120s default, 600s hard cap), shell operator detection (→ ModelRetry requiring approval), proc.kill() on timeout with ModelRetry for self-correction, SIGINT-first on POSIX before SIGKILL, interrupt hook registration in TurnEngine.cancel().

pydantic_ai_2_impl.pattern: FunctionTool with timeout=30 + non-interactive env + interruptible subprocess — prevents LLM commands from hanging, with ModelRetry on timeout for self-correction.
pydantic_ai_2_impl.why_now: ai-factory's LLMs hang when they generate commands that block on input (e.g. git commit, pip install without --no-input). _run_proc at factory/common/subprocess.py:41 has a 300s timeout but no _NONINTERACTIVE_ENV, no shell operator detection, no SIGINT interrupt hook — only SIGKILL on timeout without recovery context. A single bad command either hangs until the 300s cap (wasting context window budget) or is SIGKILLed without surfacing the error to the LLM for self-correction. OpenWorker's shell.py proves that _NONINTERACTIVE_ENV + 120s/600s timeout bounds + SIGINT-on-timeout + ModelRetry for self-correction recovers the turn instead of crashing. This is why 'LLMs keep failing' — the harness dies on a bad command instead of recovering.
pydantic_ai_2_impl.harness_gap: factory/common/subprocess.py:41 — _run_proc's subprocess.run(argv, timeout=TOOL_SUBPROCESS_TIMEOUT=300) call lacks _NONINTERACTIVE_ENV (no GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, PIP_NO_INPUT=1, DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive), no shell operator detection (;, &, |, >, <, `, $(), newlines to no ModelRetry requiring approval), and on timeout (line 48) uses SIGKILL proc.kill() (line 51) without SIGINT-first graceful recovery. factory/common/subprocess.py:69 — _run_tool wraps the subprocess call with error envelope (line 83) but adds no non-interactive env or operator detection. factory/tools/shell.py — the dedicated bash tool wrapper (analogous to OpenWorker tools/shell.py) does not exist; the bash MCP tool is a built-in opencode tool with no ai-factory safety layer. Adopt: _NONINTERACTIVE_ENV at factory/common/subprocess.py:42 (env= parameter), operator detection at factory/common/subprocess.py:22 (new _OPERATORS check in _run_proc), timeout bounds 120s/600s override at factory/common/subprocess.py:26 (TOOL_SUBPROCESS_TIMEOUT), SIGINT-first on POSIX then proc.kill() at factory/common/subprocess.py:51 on timeout with ModelRetry for self-correction, interrupt hook registration in TurnEngine.cancel().
